💭 Ever stared at your model decoding a long sequence and thought:

"Why is this so slow?!" 🤯  
Traditional attention compares every token with every other token. Quadratic complexity hits hard as sequences grow…  
Enter Sparse-K Attention — selectively focusing on the most relevant tokens.  
Less work

Same results

Much faster



I recently integrated Sparse-K into llama.cpp, and here’s what actually worked.  
Old way: Every token attends to every token → O(n²)

Sparse-K: Attend only to top-K tokens → O(n × K)
Small sequences? Barely notice.

Long sequences? 2–3× speedup without hurting accuracy.



Think about it: why waste cycles on tokens that don’t matter?

articles.description:
What is RAG in Simple Terms?
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large language models (LLMs) to pull in relevant external data at inference time, rather than rely solely on their internal parameters.
Retrieval Step: Given a user query, fetch the most relevant pieces of information (documents, paragraphs, embeddings) from an external knowledge base.
Augmentation Step: Pass that retrieved information, along with the user’s query, into the LLM as context.
Generation Step: The LLM synthesises a coherent response using both its internal knowledge and the fresh retrieved data.
This blend of retrieval + generation ensures answers are not only contextually relevant, but also grounded in explicit data rather than purely model memory.
Type 1: Naive RAG

articles.author: Sergey Sobolevski
articles.description:
Hey everyone,
I've been trading crypto and stocks for years, and it started as a rush but turned into pure stress. Nights spent glued to screens, juggling a bunch of apps: one for charts, another for risk calcs, something else for trends. I felt like I was drowning in data—exciting at first, then total burnout. Missed opportunities because I couldn't connect the dots fast enough. Frustrating losses I didn't see coming. I remember one bad trade that wiped out weeks of gains, and I thought, "There has to be a simpler way."
Then I came across the nof1.ai project- and it flipped everything. Seeing how AI could trade successfully, analyzing data with that kind of precision, made me realize: this is the future. It inspired me to build my own thing, Stockio.ai. It wasn't some corporate gig; it was me, coding late nights, testing on my own trades, fixing what broke me. Now it's a single platform that analyzes charts based on real market data for cryptocurrencies and stocks. It spots patterns you might miss and suggests positions like Hold, Short, or Long based on what's happening right now. Over the last 2 months, out of about 400 suggestions, only 4 were off- real results that have helped me make better calls and cut down on mistakes.
It's been eye-opening how AI can bring clarity to the chaos. No more app-hopping for me- just smarter decisions and less stress. Curious if others have had similar experiences with AI tools in trading. What's been your biggest frustration with charts or market analysis? Have you tried building or using something like this?
Cheers,
Ssobolevski
Founder of Stockio.ai
articles.title: I Built an AI Platform After Getting Burned Out on Trading Charts – Inspired by nof1.ai
